```{python}
# | tags: [setup]
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
import board
import charts
from board import HELP, MA_WINDOWS, tip
from charts import GREEN, INK, PURPLE, RED, WEEKEND_BREAK, html_table, plain, signed

px_all, meta, M = board.load()
SP = board.load_sp500()
MACRO = board.load_macro()
NAMES = meta.get("dashboard_names", {})


def verdict(study: dict, higher_is_claim: bool = True) -> str:
    """One-line read on whether an event study supports its claim.

    ratio_median > 1 means the conditional outcome runs bigger than baseline.
    """
    if not study or not study.get("n"):
        return "<span class='stamp'>no events</span>"
    r = study.get("ratio_median")
    if r is None:
        return "<span class='stamp'>n/a</span>"
    supports = (r > 1.05) if higher_is_claim else (r < 0.95)
    cls = "up" if supports else "down"
    word = "supports" if supports else "does not support"
    return (f"<span class='{cls}'><b>{word}</b></span> — {study['n']} events, "
            f"median {study['median']} vs baseline {study['baseline_median']} "
            f"(×{r}), {study['pct_above_baseline_median']}% above baseline")


def series(ticker):
    return px_all[px_all["ticker"] == ticker]


def note(text):
    return Markdown(f"::: {{.stamp}}\n{text}\n:::")
```

## Breadth

```{python}
if not SP or SP.get("breadth") is None:
    display(Markdown(
        "S&P 500 breadth is missing. `scripts/fetch_sp500.py` runs best-effort — "
        "it pulls ~500 tickers and is allowed to fail without taking the board "
        "down. Re-run the workflow to try again."))
else:
    b = SP["breadth"]
    fig = go.Figure()
    for col, label, color in [("pct_above_20", "% > 20d", "#3498db"),
                              ("pct_above_50", "% > 50d", "#e67e22"),
                              ("pct_above_200", "% > 200d", PURPLE)]:
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=b["date"], y=b[col], mode="lines", name=label,
                                 line=dict(color=color, width=1.6)))
    # 50% is the line between "most stocks participating" and "most not".
    fig.add_hline(y=50, line_dash="dot", line_color="#b9c2cc")
    fig.update_layout(height=380, margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=30, b=26),
                      template="plotly_white", yaxis=dict(side="right", range=[0, 100]),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.0, yanchor="bottom", x=0),
                      xaxis=dict(rangebreaks=WEEKEND_BREAK))
    fig.show(config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False})
```

```{python}
if SP and SP.get("breadth") is not None:
    last = SP["breadth"].iloc[-1]
    cards = []
    for col, label, key in [("pct_above_20", "% > 20d SMA", "breadth_20"),
                            ("pct_above_50", "% > 50d SMA", "breadth_50"),
                            ("pct_above_200", "% > 200d SMA", "breadth_200"),
                            ("pct_up", "% up on day", None)]:
        v = last[col]
        cls = "up" if v >= 50 else "down"
        lbl = tip(label, key) if key else label
        cards.append(f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">{lbl}</div>'
                     f'<div class="value {cls}">{v:.0f}%</div>'
                     f'<div class="delta stamp">of {int(last["n"])}</div></div>')
    display(HTML(f'<div class="stat-strip">{"".join(cards)}</div>'))
```

::: {.stamp}
Share of S&P 500 members above their own moving average. Above ~60% supports an
uptrend; below ~40% says the rally is narrowing to fewer stocks even when the
index looks fine.
:::

## New highs / lows

```{python}
if not SP or SP.get("highlow") is None:
    display(Markdown("52-week high/low counts unavailable — see the Breadth tab."))
else:
    hl = SP["highlow"]
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=hl["date"], y=hl["new_highs"], name="New highs",
                         marker_color=GREEN))
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=hl["date"], y=-hl["new_lows"], name="New lows",
                         marker_color=RED))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=hl["date"], y=hl["net"], mode="lines", name="Net",
                             line=dict(color=INK, width=1.4)))
    fig.update_layout(height=380, margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=30, b=26),
                      template="plotly_white", barmode="relative",
                      yaxis=dict(side="right"),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.0, yanchor="bottom", x=0),
                      xaxis=dict(rangebreaks=WEEKEND_BREAK))
    fig.show(config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False})

    latest = hl.iloc[-1]
    display(HTML(
        f'<div class="stat-strip">'
        f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">New 52w highs</div>'
        f'<div class="value up">{int(latest["new_highs"])}</div></div>'
        f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">New 52w lows</div>'
        f'<div class="value down">{int(latest["new_lows"])}</div></div>'
        f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">{tip("Net", "nh_nl")}</div>'
        f'<div class="value {"up" if latest["net"] >= 0 else "down"}">'
        f'{int(latest["net"]):+d}</div></div></div>'))
```

::: {.stamp}
Net highs minus lows. Negative while the index makes new highs is the classic
divergence warning — the rally thinning out underneath.
:::

## Housing corr

```{python}
if not MACRO or MACRO.get("corr") is None:
    display(Markdown("Macro studies unavailable — `scripts/fetch_macro.py` runs best-effort."))
else:
    from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
    c = MACRO["corr"]
    h = MACRO["meta"]["hgx"]
    view = c.tail(2600)  # ~10 years, enough to see the episodes

    fig = make_subplots(rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, row_heights=[0.68, 0.32],
                        vertical_spacing=0.04)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=view["date"], y=view["spx"], mode="lines", name="SPX",
                             line=dict(color=INK, width=1.2)), row=1, col=1)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=view["date"], y=view["corr10_px"], mode="lines",
                             name="corr10 (price)", line=dict(color=RED, width=1)),
                  row=2, col=1)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=view["date"], y=view["corr10"], mode="lines",
                             name="corr10 (returns)", line=dict(color="#3498db", width=1)),
                  row=2, col=1)
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_dash="dot", line_color="#7b8794", row=2, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(type="log", side="right", row=1, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(side="right", range=[-1.05, 1.05], row=2, col=1)
    fig.update_layout(height=470, margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=30, b=26),
                      template="plotly_white",
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.0, yanchor="bottom", x=0),
                      xaxis2=dict(rangebreaks=WEEKEND_BREAK))
    fig.show(config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False})

    cur = h["current"]
    cards = [
        ("corr10 (returns)", f"{cur['corr10_returns']:+.2f}", cur["negative_returns"]),
        ("corr10 (price)", f"{cur['corr10_price']:+.2f}", cur["negative_price"]),
    ]
    tiles = "".join(
        f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">{lbl}</div>'
        f'<div class="value {"down" if neg else "up"}">{val}</div>'
        f'<div class="delta stamp">{"negative" if neg else "positive"}</div></div>'
        for lbl, val, neg in cards)
    tiles += (f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">Price corr 5d ago</div>'
              f'<div class="value">{cur["corr10_price_5d_ago"]:+.2f}</div>'
              f'<div class="delta stamp">now {cur["corr10_price"]:+.2f}</div></div>')
    display(HTML(f'<div class="stat-strip">{tiles}</div>'))
```

::: {.stamp}
10-day correlation of the S&P 500 to the PHLX Housing index (^HGX), from
`{python} MACRO["meta"]["hgx"]["start"] if MACRO else "n/a"`. Two definitions
are shown because they disagree: charting packages usually correlate **closing
prices**, while correlating **returns** is the sounder read — over 10 bars a
price correlation mostly measures shared trend.
:::

```{python}
if MACRO and MACRO.get("corr") is not None:
    h = MACRO["meta"]["hgx"]
    rows = []
    for key in ("returns", "price"):
        s = h[key]["episode_starts"]
        rows.append(
            f"<tr><td>{key}</td><td>{h[key]['pct_days_negative']}%</td>"
            f"<td>{h[key]['episodes']}</td>"
            f"<td>{verdict(s, higher_is_claim=True)}</td></tr>")
    display(HTML(
        "<div class='table-wrap'><table class='board'><thead><tr>"
        "<th>Definition</th><th>Days negative</th><th>Episodes</th>"
        f"<th>Claim: negative corr → volatility within {h['forward_days']}d</th>"
        f"</tr></thead><tbody>{''.join(rows)}</tbody></table></div>"))
```

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="What the history actually says about this signal"}
The claim attached to this indicator is that stretches of negative correlation
tend to be followed by market volatility. Tested over the full ^HGX history,
**it isn't supported** — on either definition, at 10/21/63-day horizons, and
whether the outcome is realized volatility, forward drawdown, or absolute move.
Forward volatility after a negative reading runs at or *below* baseline
(roughly ×0.86–0.97), and forward drawdowns are shallower, not deeper.

These are overlapping forward windows, so treat them as descriptive rather than
significance-tested — but the effect doesn't merely fail to reach significance,
it points the other way across every specification tried.

The indicator is here because it's worth watching a housing/equity divergence
on its own merits. It just shouldn't be read as a volatility warning.
:::

## Macro lockstep

```{python}
if not MACRO or MACRO.get("lockstep") is None:
    display(Markdown("Macro studies unavailable — `scripts/fetch_macro.py` runs best-effort."))
else:
    from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
    lk = MACRO["lockstep"]
    L = MACRO["meta"]["lockstep"]
    view = lk.tail(2600)

    fig = make_subplots(rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, row_heights=[0.55, 0.45],
                        vertical_spacing=0.05)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=view["date"], y=view["pc1_share"], mode="lines",
                             name="Lockstep (PC1 share)", line=dict(color=PURPLE, width=1.4)),
                  row=1, col=1)
    fig.add_hline(y=L["decile_hi"], line_dash="dash", line_color="#e74c3c", row=1, col=1)
    fig.add_hline(y=L["decile_lo"], line_dash="dot", line_color="#b9c2cc", row=1, col=1)
    for col, name, color in (("c_spx_tyx", "SPX·30Y", "#3498db"),
                             ("c_spx_dxy", "SPX·DXY", "#e67e22"),
                             ("c_tyx_dxy", "30Y·DXY", "#18bc9c")):
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=view["date"], y=view[col], mode="lines", name=name,
                                 line=dict(color=color, width=1)), row=2, col=1)
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_dash="dot", line_color="#7b8794", row=2, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(side="right", row=1, col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(side="right", range=[-1.05, 1.05], row=2, col=1)
    fig.update_layout(height=470, margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=30, b=26),
                      template="plotly_white",
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.0, yanchor="bottom", x=0))
    fig.show(config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False})

    t = MACRO["meta"].get("tyx", {})
    tiles = [
        ("Lockstep now", f"{L['current_pc1']:.2f}",
         f"{L['current_pct_rank']:.0f}th pct", L["current_pc1"] >= L["decile_hi"]),
        ("Aligned above", f"{L['decile_hi']:.2f}", "top decile", False),
        ("30Y yield", f"{t.get('current', float('nan')):.2f}%",
         f"{t.get('pct_off_5y_high', 0):+.2f}% vs 5y high", False),
        ("30Y vs all-time", f"{t.get('pct_of_all_time_high', 0):.0f}%",
         f"ATH {t.get('all_time_high', 0):.2f}% in {str(t.get('all_time_high_date',''))[:4]}", False),
    ]
    display(HTML('<div class="stat-strip">' + "".join(
        f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">{lbl}</div>'
        f'<div class="value {"up" if hot else ""}">{val}</div>'
        f'<div class="delta stamp">{sub}</div></div>'
        for lbl, val, sub, hot in tiles) + "</div>"))
```

```{python}
if MACRO and MACRO.get("lockstep") is not None:

        for lbl, key, claim in [
            (f"Aligned → bigger {L['forward_days']}d move (either direction)",
             "abs_move_when_aligned", True),
            (f"Aligned → higher {L['forward_days']}d realized vol",
             "vol_when_aligned", True),
            (f"Dispersed → smaller {L['forward_days']}d move",
             "abs_move_when_dispersed", False)])
    display(HTML(

        f"<th>Since {L['start']}</th></tr></thead><tbody>{rows}</tbody></table></div>"))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How the lockstep score works, and what the history says"}
"All three moving in lockstep" is a statement about a single common factor
driving the S&P 500, the 30-year yield, and the dollar. That is what the first
principal component's share of variance measures: **0.33** means the three are
independent, **1.00** means they're one thing wearing three hats. It's computed
on a `{python} MACRO["meta"]["lockstep"]["window"] if MACRO else 60`-day
rolling correlation matrix of daily innovations — log returns for the S&P and
the dollar, and a **first difference** for the 30-year, because a percentage
"return" on a yield level would make the correlation depend on the level rather
than the move.

Tested back to 1977, the framework holds up: when alignment sits in its top
decile, the next month's absolute S&P move runs about ×1.14 baseline and
realized volatility ×1.20 — and the converse also holds, with dispersed periods
running ×0.79. Measuring *absolute* move is the right test for a claim about
"melt ups and meltdowns alike".

On the 30-year "pushing back toward all time highs": it is at its **10-year**
high, which is the useful sense of the claim. It is not near its all-time high —
that was 15.21% in October 1981, and today's level is about a third of it.
:::

## RS boards

```{python}
RS_SPEC = [
    ("rs_pct",      tip("RS rank", "rs_1m"),               lambda v: plain(v, 0)),
    ("ret_1d",      "1D",                                  lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
    ("ret_1m",      tip("1M", "ret_1m"),                   lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
    ("rs_1m",       tip("RS 1M", "rs_1m"),                 lambda v: signed(v, 1)),
    ("rs_3m",       tip("RS 3M", "rs_3m"),                 lambda v: signed(v, 1)),
    ("pct_off_52w", tip("Off 52w hi", "pct_off_52w_high"), lambda v: signed(v, 1)),
]

out = []
for group_name, tickers in meta.get("dashboard_groups", {}).items():
    sub = board.rs_rank(M, tickers)
    if sub.empty:
        continue
    out.append(f"<h4>{group_name}</h4>")
    out.append(html_table(
        sub, RS_SPEC,
        first_cell=lambda tk, r: f"{tk} <span class='stamp'>{NAMES.get(tk, '')}</span>"))
```

## Benchmarks

```{python}
MATRIX_TICKERS = ["SPY", "QQQ", "DIA", "IWM", "RSP", "IJH", "IJR"]
mm = M[M.index.isin(MATRIX_TICKERS)].reindex([t for t in MATRIX_TICKERS if t in M.index])


def ma_cell(v):
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and pd.isna(v)):
        return "—"
    return ('<span class="pill up">above</span>' if v
            else '<span class="pill down">below</span>')


MM_SPEC = ([(f"above_{w}", str(w), ma_cell) for w in MA_WINDOWS] +
           [("ret_ytd", tip("YTD", "ret_ytd"), lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
            ("pct_off_52w", tip("Off 52w hi", "pct_off_52w_high"), lambda v: signed(v, 1))])

table = html_table(mm, MM_SPEC, first_header=tip("MA matrix", "ma_matrix"))

# "Percent positive" — breadth across the benchmark list itself.
pos = []
for w in MA_WINDOWS:
    vals = [v for v in mm[f"above_{w}"] if v is not None]
    pos.append(f"<td>{(100 * sum(vals) / len(vals)):.0f}%</td>" if vals else "<td>—</td>")
table = table.replace("</tbody>",
                      f"<tr class='summary'><td>Percent positive</td>{''.join(pos)}"
                      f"<td></td><td></td></tr></tbody>")
display(HTML(table))

PERF_SPEC = [
    ("ret_1w",  tip("1W", "ret_1w"),   lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
    ("ret_1m",  tip("1M", "ret_1m"),   lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
    ("ret_3m",  tip("3M", "ret_3m"),   lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
    ("ret_6m",  tip("6M", "ret_6m"),   lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
    ("ret_ytd", tip("YTD", "ret_ytd"), lambda v: signed(v * 100, 1)),
    ("rsi",     tip("RSI", "rsi"),     lambda v: plain(v, 0)),
]
display(Markdown("**Trailing returns**"))
HTML(html_table(M[M.index.isin(MATRIX_TICKERS)].sort_values("ret_1m", ascending=False),
                PERF_SPEC))
```

## Risk on/off

```{python}
# TLT vs SPY, both normalized to 100 at the start of the window. Rising = bonds
# outperforming (risk-off); falling = equities leading (risk-on).
win = 126
tlt, spy = series("TLT").tail(win), series("SPY").tail(win)
fig = go.Figure()
if not tlt.empty and not spy.empty:
    j = (tlt[["date", "close"]].rename(columns={"close": "tlt"})
         .merge(spy[["date", "close"]].rename(columns={"close": "spy"}), on="date"))
    ratio = j["tlt"] / j["spy"]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=j["date"], y=ratio / ratio.iloc[0] * 100, mode="lines",
                             name="TLT / SPY", line=dict(color=PURPLE, width=2)))
    fig.add_hline(y=100, line_dash="dot", line_color="#b9c2cc")
fig.update_layout(height=320, margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=30, b=26), template="plotly_white",
                  yaxis=dict(side="right"), showlegend=False,
                  xaxis=dict(rangebreaks=WEEKEND_BREAK))
fig.show(config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False})
```

::: {.stamp}
TLT (20+ year Treasuries) relative to SPY, normalized to 100 six months ago.
Rising = bonds outperforming stocks (risk-off). Read the slope, not the level.
:::
